intro.title: Build checkout API with idempotency keys
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a checkout API endpoint in Node.js that uses idempotency keys to prevent duplicate payments. You will learn how idempotency ensures that the same request can be safely repeated without unintended side effects, such as charging a customer twice. The main technologies involved include Express.js for routing, an in-memory object to simulate storing idempotency keys, and HTTP POST requests. By the end, you'll have a functional API that handles payment requests idempotently, a key concept for reliable financial transactions.
intro.usecase: Idempotency keys are essential in payment processing systems where duplicate charges must be prevented. When a user clicks 'Pay Now' multiple times due to network delays or impatience, idempotent APIs ensure only one transaction occurs. This pattern is used by e-commerce platforms like Shopify, payment gateways like Stripe, and financial apps where checkout reliability is critical. Developers implement idempotency keys in checkout APIs to handle retries safely without creating duplicate orders or charging customers twice.
